answer: Register one timber haven per applicant on a trail for 120 days. The keeper pays a 150 token deposit and a 95 dollar license, then numbers 20 timber beams and photographs them weekly. A steel vault inside holds the guest log, and travelers sign when they shelter there. A ranger opens the vault twice to match signatures against trail counts. A forged log forfeits the deposit and bars the keeper 180 days. A haven works like a hut logbook on a long trail, where a ranger reads the names and knows who passed. Faking 10,000 havens freezes 1,500,000 tokens and costs 950,000 dollars in licenses.
